q: Pictured: canopy (awning). Which vernacular term names it?
ref: Know-How Architecture, “Building Technology: Construction Vernacular Terms” (#InstaFlashCards): term and image.
n: “Media Agua” is the vernacular for canopy (awning). Origin: Spanish media agua “half water”: a single-slope roof that sheds rain to one side only.

q: Pictured: slope. Which vernacular term names it?
ref: Know-How Architecture, “Building Technology: Construction Vernacular Terms” (#InstaFlashCards): term and image.
n: “Bahada” is the vernacular for slope. Origin: likely Spanish bajada “descent, slope”. Filipino spelling turns j into h, as in bajada, bahada.

q: Pictured: gutter. Which vernacular term names it?
ref: Know-How Architecture, “Building Technology: Construction Vernacular Terms” (#InstaFlashCards): term and image.
n: “Alulod, Kanal” is the vernacular for gutter. Origin: kanal is Spanish canal “channel”, the same word as English “canal”. Alulod is the native Filipino word for a water channel.

q: Pictured: gable roof. Which vernacular term names it?
ref: Know-How Architecture, “Building Technology: Construction Vernacular Terms” (#InstaFlashCards): term and image.
n: “Dos Aguas” is the vernacular for gable roof. Origin: Spanish dos aguas “two waters”: a roof that sheds rain to two sides.

q: Pictured: corrugated G.I. sheet. Which vernacular term names it?
ref: Know-How Architecture, “Building Technology: Construction Vernacular Terms” (#InstaFlashCards): term and image.
n: “Hiero Kanalado” is the vernacular for corrugated G.I. sheet. Origin: Spanish hierro “iron” + canalado “grooved, channelled”, so channelled iron sheet.

q: Pictured: ridge roll. Which vernacular term names it?
ref: Know-How Architecture, “Building Technology: Construction Vernacular Terms” (#InstaFlashCards): term and image.
n: “Caballete / Kaballete” is the vernacular for ridge roll. Origin: Spanish caballete “roof ridge”, literally “little horse”. The ridge runs along the roof like a horse's back.

q: Pictured: overhang (projection). Which vernacular term names it?
ref: Know-How Architecture, “Building Technology: Construction Vernacular Terms” (#InstaFlashCards): term and image.
n: “Bolada” is the vernacular for overhang (projection). Origin: Spanish voladizo/volada “jutting out”, from volar “to fly”. Filipino spelling swaps v for b.

q: Pictured: plain G.I. sheet. Which vernacular term names it?
ref: Know-How Architecture, “Building Technology: Construction Vernacular Terms” (#InstaFlashCards): term and image.
n: “Hiero Liso” is the vernacular for plain G.I. sheet. Origin: Spanish hierro “iron” + liso “smooth, plain”, so smooth iron sheet.

q: Pictured: open terrace. Which vernacular term names it?
ref: Know-How Architecture, “Building Technology: Construction Vernacular Terms” (#InstaFlashCards): term and image.
n: “Azotea” is the vernacular for open terrace. Origin: Spanish azotea “flat roof or terrace”, from Arabic as-suṭayḥa “the little flat surface”.
